nodes.label: Fundamentals of Skin Anti-Aging Overview
nodes.summary: Section overview introducing anti-aging research from genomics to apoptosis. Highlights sirtuins, stem cells, DNA repair, glycation/AGEs, telomere theory, beauty from within, sleep, senescence and epigenetics.

nodes.label: Sirtuins
nodes.summary: Longevity-associated proteins; activating/modulating sirtuins is presented as an expanding anti-aging strategy boosting cell longevity.

nodes.label: Glycation
nodes.summary: Glucose molecules react with proteins including collagen, forming AGEs that contribute to elasticity loss, wrinkles, inflammation and accelerated aging.

nodes.label: Advanced Glycation End Products
nodes.summary: Products of glucose binding to proteins such as collagen; contribute to loss of elasticity, wrinkles, inflammation, accelerated aging.

nodes.label: Collagen
nodes.summary: Skin structural protein that is attacked by glucose in glycation, forming AGEs.

nodes.label: Telomere Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: States that the faster telomeres shorten, the faster one ages biologically.

nodes.label: Beauty from Within
nodes.summary: Concept that hydrating foods and ingestible nutricosmetics protect skin internally from free radical damage.

nodes.label: Sleep Deprivation
nodes.summary: Contributes to adverse skin effects; sleep resets metabolism, repairs damaged cells and clears waste.

nodes.label: Apoptosis
nodes.summary: Programmed cell death; critical in understanding aging, embryo development and immune protection against abnormal cells.

nodes.label: Cellular Senescence
nodes.summary: State where cells stop replicating; its reversal is believed to be an important function of anti-aging products.

nodes.label: Epigenetics
nodes.summary: Science challenging the assumption that aging is unstoppable deterioration; genomics increasingly used by skin care industry.

nodes.label: Skin Aging
nodes.summary: Natural progressive process of the skin determined by intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

nodes.label: Free Radicals
nodes.summary: Unstable reactive molecules whose activity damages cells and affects cell longevity.

nodes.label: Theories of Aging: Skin Anti-Aging at the Tipping Point
nodes.summary: Reviews fifteen mainstream theories of aging, grouped into DNA damage theories and built-in (programmed) breakdown theories. Concludes the most established are free radical, mitochondrial, hormonal and telomere theories, with no unified theory and caloric restriction the only intervention shown to slow cellular time (in non-humans).

nodes.label: Intrinsic Aging
nodes.summary: Internally determined, genetically programmed component of aging, one of the additive influences on skin aging.

nodes.label: DNA Damage Theories of Aging
nodes.summary: Group of theories holding that accumulated DNA damage inhibits cell function and gene expression, leading to cell death and skin aging.

nodes.label: Programmed (Built-in Breakdown) Aging Theories
nodes.summary: Theories holding aging is a direct consequence of genetic programming, a molecular clock built into genome and cell structure.

nodes.label: Wear and Tear Theory
nodes.summary: Oldest, most outdated theory: cells and organs damaged by constant use, toxins, UV and stress leave unrepaired damage; includes immune wear-out.

nodes.label: Neuro-Endocrine Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: Aging endocrine glands governed by the hypothalamus secrete less hormone, reducing repair/regulation; receptors are downgraded and circadian hormone rhythms become irregular.

nodes.label: Hypothalamus
nodes.summary: Brain region governing hormone release; proposed site of the aging chronometer.

nodes.label: Genetic Control Theory
nodes.summary: Inherited longevity assurance genes and a biological clock determine aging; aging results from loss of capacity of dormant renewal cells to divide.

nodes.label: Free Radical Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: Most commonly held theory, proposed by Denham Harman in 1954: free radicals damage molecules causing DNA damage, protein cross-linking and age pigments.

nodes.label: Reactive Oxygen Species
nodes.summary: Oxygen radicals; by-products of mitochondrial metabolism that damage mitochondrial DNA.

nodes.label: Lipofuscin
nodes.summary: Yellow-brown 'cellular garbage' age pigment from free radical attack on membranes; excess manifests as aging spots; common in nerve and heart muscle cells.

nodes.label: Age Spots
nodes.summary: Darkening of skin areas attributed to excess lipofuscin.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: Toxins and by-products accumulate in mitochondria, reducing energy output; mitochondrial DNA damaged by oxygen radicals.

nodes.label: Mitochondria
nodes.summary: Organelles using oxygen to produce energy; weakest link in aging as they lack most cellular free radical defenses.

nodes.label: Waste Accumulation Theory
nodes.summary: Accumulation of metabolic by-products (free radicals, aldehydes, histones, lipofuscins) interferes with cell function and kills cells.

nodes.label: Hayflick Limit Theory
nodes.summary: Cells have a preset number of divisions; human fibroblasts divide about 50 times then stop, each copy poorer in quality.

nodes.label: Fibroblast
nodes.summary: Cells with limited life span; embryonic fibroblasts divide ~50 times, adult ones ~20 times.

nodes.label: Death Hormone Theory
nodes.summary: Hypothalamic aging chronometer; pituitary may release DOCH, inhibiting cell use of thyroxin and accelerating aging.

nodes.label: Thyroxin
nodes.summary: Thyroid hormone governing basal metabolism; DOCH is speculated to inhibit its use by cells.

nodes.label: Caloric Restriction
nodes.summary: Restricting calories (40-60%) extends life span in yeast, worms, flies, mice and primates; not shown to slow aging in humans; practitioners look older facially.

nodes.label: Gene Silencing
nodes.summary: Suppression of certain genes by sirtuins; loss of this function with age is linked to cancer, Alzheimer's and diabetes.

nodes.label: Cross-Linking Theory
nodes.summary: Also called glycosylation theory: abnormal cross-links between proteins/DNA irreversibly alter structures like collagen and enzymes, causing wrinkling.

nodes.label: Protein Cross-Linking
nodes.summary: Formation of abnormal bonds between proteins that reduce mobility and elasticity; cross-linking of collagen responsible for wrinkling.

nodes.label: Elastin
nodes.summary: Elastic fibers degenerate with age and are replaced by less flexible collagen; damaged by inflammation-generated free radicals.

nodes.label: Wrinkles
nodes.summary: Age-related sign caused by collagen cross-linking and inflammation-derived free radical damage to collagen and elastin.

nodes.label: Telomeres
nodes.summary: Non-coding DNA at chromosome ends that maintain genetic integrity; shorten with each division leading to senescence.

nodes.label: Telomerase
nodes.summary: Enzyme that maintains and rebuilds telomeres; found in germ and cancer cells; telomerase inhibitors may stop cancer cell division.

nodes.label: Telomere Shortening
nodes.summary: Progressive loss of telomeres with each cell division, leading to instability, senescence and death.

nodes.label: Glycation Theory
nodes.summary: Theory attributing aging and diseases (arterial stiffening, cataracts) to glycation; predominant in medical literature due to diabetes.

nodes.label: NF-kB
nodes.summary: Inflammatory transcription factor; stimulated by AGEs; buildup in rheumatoid arthritis.

nodes.label: Mutation Accumulation and DNA/RNA Damage Theory
nodes.summary: DNA damage and mutations interfere with gene expression, proposed as an aging mechanism.

nodes.label: DNA Damage
nodes.summary: Chemical changes in DNA structure producing dysfunction; central to most aging theories.

nodes.label: Deficient Immune System/Autoimmune Theory
nodes.summary: With age the immune system fails to distinguish self from foreign proteins and antibody production declines.

nodes.label: Inflammation Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: Free radicals attack membranes producing arachidonic acid via phospholipase A2; oxidized products cause inflammation, a self-perpetuating cycle accelerating aging.

nodes.label: Inflammation
nodes.summary: Response that combats infection but in excess accelerates aging and damages collagen/elastin; triggered by smoke, UV, pollution, stress, poor sleep.

nodes.label: Arachidonic Acid
nodes.summary: Produced from cell membranes by phospholipase A2; oxidized into pro-inflammatory chemicals.

nodes.label: Phospholipase A2
nodes.summary: Enzyme triggered when skin is traumatized; releases arachidonic acid from membranes.

nodes.label: Inflammatory Cytokines
nodes.summary: Destructive cell-signalling chemicals (TNF-alpha, IL-6) that increase systemically with age and contribute to degenerative disease.

nodes.label: TNF-alpha
nodes.summary: Tumor necrosis factor-alpha, a cytokine contributing to inflammation.

nodes.label: Interleukin-6
nodes.summary: Cytokine contributing to inflammation.

nodes.label: C-Reactive Protein
nodes.summary: Elevated blood levels in aging people indicate inflammatory disorder.

nodes.label: UV Radiation
nodes.summary: External trigger of inflammation and additive influence on skin aging.

nodes.label: Oxidative Stress
nodes.summary: Chronic oxidant stress, alongside inflammation, ravages aging skin.

nodes.label: Denham Harman
nodes.summary: Scientist who proposed the free radical theory of aging in 1954.

nodes.label: The Cellular Water Principle
nodes.summary: Argues that loss of intracellular water is the final common pathway of aging and disease. Reviews definitions and classifications of aging theories, Nagy's membrane hypothesis, and clinical bioelectrical impedance data showing dietary supplementation raised intracellular water, phase angle and BMR.

nodes.label: Cellular Water Principle
nodes.summary: Optimizing intracellular and extracellular tissue water to achieve cellular water homeostasis improves metabolism, health and dermal appearance; about getting water into cells, not just drinking it.

nodes.label: Intracellular Water
nodes.summary: Water within the cytosol (cell water volume); must be kept steady for metabolism and youthful appearance; reduced in elderly, especially diseased persons.

nodes.label: Extracellular Water
nodes.summary: Water outside cell membranes acting as reservoir for intracellular water; divided into interstitial, plasma and transcellular compartments.

nodes.label: Edematous Water
nodes.summary: 'Wasted water' in inflamed or injured tissue manifesting as bloating, puffiness and swelling; not available to cells.

nodes.label: Total Body Water
nodes.summary: Sum of intracellular and extracellular water (ICW+ECW=TBW).

nodes.label: Cellular Dehydration
nodes.summary: Progressive loss of intracellular water with accumulation of dry mass; increases free radical damage efficiency and slows enzymes; final common pathway of aging.

nodes.label: Membrane Hypothesis of Aging
nodes.summary: Nagy's hypothesis: free-radical cross-linking damages plasma membranes, decreasing potassium permeability, causing colloid condensation, water loss, enzyme inhibition and lipofuscin accumulation.

nodes.label: Plasma Membrane
nodes.summary: Cell membrane that suffers cumulative structural and functional damage with age per the membrane hypothesis.

nodes.label: Strehler's Criteria of Aging
nodes.summary: Bernard Strehler's definition: aging is destructive, progressive, intrinsically determined and universal.

nodes.label: Esposito Classification of Aging Theories
nodes.summary: 1983 classification dividing aging theories into causal, systemic and evolutionary groups.

nodes.label: Hayflick's Entropy View of Aging
nodes.summary: Hayflick defines aging as increasing molecular disorder (entropy), stochastic and thermodynamically driven, not gene driven.

nodes.label: Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis
nodes.summary: BIA diagnostic tool measuring TBW, ICW, ECW, basal metabolic rate and phase angle; used on over 1500 patients aged 25-85.

nodes.label: Phase Angle
nodes.summary: Arctangent of reactance/resistance; indicator of cell vitality and membrane integrity; decreases with age; 65% of 40 supplemented patients showed increase.

nodes.label: Basal Metabolic Rate
nodes.summary: Rate of resting energy use; increased in 55% of supplemented patients, correlating with phase angle (p<0.05).

nodes.label: Dietary Supplementation
nodes.summary: Comprehensive regimen of cell/connective tissue nutrients (glucosamine, amino acids, lecithin, EFAs, vitamins, sirtuin activators); 12 weeks raised ICW in 57.5% of patients.

nodes.label: Glucosamine
nodes.summary: Cell and connective tissue-building, hydrating nutrient recommended in the supplement regimen.

nodes.label: Lecithin
nodes.summary: Phosphatidylcholine; hydrating nutrient whose dietary deficiency is linked to cellular dehydration.

nodes.label: Essential Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Hydrating nutrients included in the cellular water supplement regimen.

nodes.label: Sirtuin Activators
nodes.summary: Nutrients listed among hydrating, cell-building supplements.

nodes.label: Successful Aging
nodes.summary: Rowe and Kahn: low disease risk, high mental/physical function, active engagement; Murad extends to 'Inclusive Health'.

nodes.label: Anti-Senescence: Managing Cellular Functions
nodes.summary: Presents cellular anti-senescence as a 'single-bullet' skin anti-aging approach. Covers senescence vs apoptosis, enzyme dysfunction (oxidative stress, peroxisomes, immunosenescence, AGEs, ubiquitin-proteasome system, MFRTA), anhydrobiosis and osmoprotection, new osmoprotective glutaminylglutamine amide peptide derivatives with formulations, and consumer marketing of enzyme biology.

nodes.label: Cellular Anti-Senescence
nodes.summary: 'Single-bullet' anti-aging approach patented by Gupta and Walker that manages cellular senescence to retard skin aging.

nodes.label: Antagonistic Pleiotropy
nodes.summary: One gene controlling multiple traits, at least one beneficial and one detrimental; apoptosis and senescence may be examples.

nodes.label: Keratinocyte
nodes.summary: Epidermal cell; senescent keratinocytes accumulate with age.

nodes.label: Redox Active Metals
nodes.summary: Iron, copper, chromium, cobalt undergo redox cycling producing superoxide and nitric oxide radicals.

nodes.label: Superoxide Dismutase
nodes.summary: Major metal-containing antioxidant enzyme; activity reduced by free radical damage.

nodes.label: Catalase
nodes.summary: Metal-containing antioxidant enzyme balancing oxidative stress.

nodes.label: Glutathione
nodes.summary: Endogenous antioxidant balancing cellular oxidative stress; reacts with prostaglandin J2 cyclopentenone.

nodes.label: Paraoxonase 1
nodes.summary: Anti-atherosclerotic enzyme preventing lipoperoxide accumulation and LDL lipid oxidation.

nodes.label: Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Exogenous antioxidant supplementation needed as endogenous defenses decline during senescence.

nodes.label: Peroxisome
nodes.summary: Organelle for hydrogen peroxide metabolism and fatty acid beta-oxidation; its ROS are major contributors to oxidative stress and aging.

nodes.label: Immunosenescence
nodes.summary: Age-related decline in immune response mainly due to T-cell decline.

nodes.label: T-Cell
nodes.summary: Immune cell; low ROS required for survival, high ROS cause apoptosis/necrosis; decline drives immunosenescence.

nodes.label: Resveratrol
nodes.summary: Found capable of counteracting immunosenescence leading to cellular rejuvenation.

nodes.label: Amadori Product
nodes.summary: Early glycation product formed when reducing sugars react non-enzymatically with protein amino groups.

nodes.label: Receptor for Advanced Glycation End Products
nodes.summary: RAGE; interaction with AGEs elicits oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory gene activation.

nodes.label: Proteasome
nodes.summary: 26S barrel-shaped multi-subunit protease complex with core and two caps; activity decreases up to age 50; malfunction may contribute to skin aging.

nodes.label: Ubiquitin
nodes.summary: 76-amino-acid protein (~8500 amu) marking proteins for proteolysis; 96% identical between human and yeast; C-terminal gly-gly binding site.

nodes.label: Ubiquitin-Proteasome Pathway
nodes.summary: Major intracellular protein degradation system: E1, E2, E3 enzymes tag proteins with ubiquitin for proteasome degradation; controls cell division, signaling, gene regulation.

nodes.label: Proteolysis
nodes.summary: Protein breakdown essential to cell survival and turnover; via lysosomes, ubiquitin-proteasome pathway and calpains.

nodes.label: Calpains
nodes.summary: Proteases breaking down proteins that give cells shape and stability.

nodes.label: Lysosome
nodes.summary: Cell component containing proteases that break down proteins.

nodes.label: Cyclooxygenase-2
nodes.summary: Inducible pro-inflammatory enzyme catalyzing prostaglandin biosynthesis from arachidonic acid; triggered by ubiquitinated protein aggregates.

nodes.label: Prostaglandin J2
nodes.summary: COX-2 product with cyclopentenone ring that increases ubiquitinated proteins and COX-2, a self-destructive feedback loop.

nodes.label: Neurodegenerative Disorders
nodes.summary: Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS associated with ubiquitinated protein inclusions and inflammation.

nodes.label: Molecular Chaperones
nodes.summary: Proteins that attenuate ubiquitinated protein accumulation; proposed for skin aging, inflammation and wound healing.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial Free Radical Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: MFRTA: aging caused by macromolecule damage from mitochondrial ROS; influential for 50 years but challenged by long-lived species studies.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial Biogenesis
nodes.summary: Mitochondriogenesis; its promotion is critical to preventing aging.

nodes.label: Hydroxyl Radical
nodes.summary: Highly reactive species derived from superoxide; initiator of aging.

nodes.label: Peroxynitrite
nodes.summary: Reactive species derived from nitric oxide; initiator of aging.

nodes.label: Superoxide
nodes.summary: Physiological free radical, mostly harmless itself but precursor of hydroxyl radicals.

nodes.label: Nitric Oxide
nodes.summary: Physiological free radical precursor of peroxynitrite.

nodes.label: Anhydrobiosis
nodes.summary: 'Life without water': survival in quiescent extreme desiccation found in bacteria, archaea, fungi, invertebrates and resurrection plants; platform for anti-aging osmoprotective therapies.

nodes.label: High-Density Water
nodes.summary: Highly reactive intracellular water state; its increase generates ROS and impairs repair, leading to aging.

nodes.label: Low-Density Water
nodes.summary: Low-reactivity water predominant in macromolecular-crowded cytoplasm.

nodes.label: Osmoprotection
nodes.summary: Adaptation via compatible solutes protecting cells from osmotic stress; offered as therapy for collagen synthesis, inflammation, wrinkles, brightening, age spots and acne.

nodes.label: Osmotic Stress
nodes.summary: Loss of internal cellular pressure from water loss causing aged skin appearance.

nodes.label: Hyperosmolarity
nodes.summary: Above 300 mOsm induces secretion of IL-8, IL-6, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha via PP2A methylation shift activating NF-kB.

nodes.label: Human Polynucleotide Phosphorylase
nodes.summary: hPNPase (old-35): RNA-degrading enzyme upregulated in senescence; promotes ROS, activates NF-kB and IL-6/IL-8; proposed target.

nodes.label: Glycine Betaine
nodes.summary: Most active natural osmoprotectant for E. coli; found in urine and accumulated by kidney medulla cells.

nodes.label: Proline Betaine
nodes.summary: Anti-senescence osmoprotectant identified in human urine.

nodes.label: Dimethylthetin
nodes.summary: Sulfonium analog of glycine betaine equally effective as osmoprotectant for E. coli.

nodes.label: Trehalose
nodes.summary: Non-reducing disaccharide osmoprotectant from anhydrobiotic organisms; used to preserve foods, enzymes, vaccines and cells dehydrated.

nodes.label: Ectoine
nodes.summary: Compatible solute osmoprotectant; NADA is its precursor.

nodes.label: Carnitine
nodes.summary: Osmoprotectant; topical carnitine in dry eye offers osmoprotection and modulates immune/inflammatory responses.

nodes.label: Taurine
nodes.summary: Organic osmolyte accumulated by kidney medulla cells.

nodes.label: Proline
nodes.summary: Amino acid osmoprotectant; increased tenfold-fivefold under salt stress.

nodes.label: N-Acetylglutaminylglutamine Amide
nodes.summary: Dipeptide osmolyte discovered in Sinorhizobium meliloti at high osmolarity; lead for new anti-senescence peptides.

nodes.label: Glutaminylglutamine Amide Derivatives
nodes.summary: Gupta-Walker osmoprotective anti-senescence peptide derivatives for topical skin anti-aging; formulated at pH 4.5-6.5.

nodes.label: Aloesin
nodes.summary: Key osmoprotective active in Aloe vera; derivatives with amino acids and peptides reported.

nodes.label: Aloe Vera
nodes.summary: Plant source of aloesin.

nodes.label: Dry Eye Syndrome
nodes.summary: Common disorder in which tear film hyperosmolarity drives ocular surface inflammation.

nodes.label: Dry Skin
nodes.summary: Excessive skin dryness linked to hyperosmolarity and senescence; target of osmoprotective agents.

nodes.label: Anti-Aging Cream
nodes.summary: Example formulation with niacinamide salicylate, ethyl lactate, paeonol, carnosine, arbutin and peptide compound (III).

nodes.label: Niacinamide
nodes.summary: Used as hydroxycitrate (2.2%) and salicylate (4.0%) in the anti-aging cream.

nodes.label: Paeonol
nodes.summary: Used in anti-aging cream (1.5%) and anti-inflammatory gel (0.5%).

nodes.label: Magnolol
nodes.summary: Used with honokiol in anti-inflammatory gel and in anti-aging cream (0.2%).

nodes.label: Carnosine
nodes.summary: Used at 0.1% in the anti-aging cream.

nodes.label: Arbutin
nodes.summary: Used at 0.5% in the anti-aging cream.

nodes.label: Ethyl Lactate
nodes.summary: Solvent base: 15% in cream and 96% in anti-inflammatory transparent gel.

nodes.label: Enzyme Biology-Based Skin Care Marketing
nodes.summary: Challenge of explaining slow, cumulative enzyme-based anti-senescence to consumers confused by 'percentage claims' and immediate-results marketing.

nodes.label: Papain
nodes.summary: Fruit enzyme known to professionals for gentle exfoliation.

nodes.label: Bromelain
nodes.summary: Fruit enzyme used for gentle exfoliation and smoothing.

nodes.label: Glycation, Proteasome Activation, and Telomere Maintenance
nodes.summary: Reviews glycation (AGE formation, measurement by AGE-Reader autofluorescence, anti-glycation and deglycation ingredients incl. Albizia julibrissin), the proteasome/UPS and autophagy as cellular clearance targets, and telomere/telomerase/shelterin biology with cosmetic telomere-protecting actives. Stresses the three topics are interconnected.

nodes.label: Schiff Base
nodes.summary: Unstable reversible bond between reducing sugar aldehyde and protein amine; first stage of AGE formation.

nodes.label: Glycotoxins
nodes.summary: Heterogeneous sugar-derived reactive molecules from diet, cigarette smoke and glycation intermediates; as important as sunlight in skin aging.

nodes.label: Methylglyoxal
nodes.summary: Reactive dicarbonyl glycotoxin (MGO) forming AGEs such as CML/CEL; overproduces H2O2 accelerating fibroblast senescence.

nodes.label: Glyoxal
nodes.summary: Reactive dicarbonyl glycotoxin (GO) from Amadori stage forming AGEs.

nodes.label: Carboxymethyl-Lysine
nodes.summary: CML: typical AGE; collagen contains three times more CML at age 80 than 20; UV oxidation accelerates CML in actinic elastosis.

nodes.label: Pentosidine
nodes.summary: AGE accumulating in long-lived collagen with age.

nodes.label: Vimentin
nodes.summary: Cytoskeletal protein that is the specific primary target of glycation in skin, reducing fibroblast contractility.

nodes.label: Diabetes
nodes.summary: Accelerates glycation and AGE accumulation; drives pharmacological research benefiting cosmetic anti-glycation.

nodes.label: AGE-Reader
nodes.summary: DiagnOptics device measuring skin AGEs noninvasively by autofluorescence at 370±50 nm; readings rise 0.023 units per year of age.

nodes.label: Glycated Hemoglobin
nodes.summary: Less invasive blood measure replacing skin biopsies for glycation severity.

nodes.label: Glyoxalase
nodes.summary: Glyoxalase-1 and -2 enzyme system detoxifying glyoxal/MGO via glutathione; overexpression extends diabetic animal lifespan; reduced by glycation.

nodes.label: Aminoguanidine
nodes.summary: Well-known benchmark anti-glycation agent.

nodes.label: Aspirin
nodes.summary: Acetylates lysine amines, blocking glycation reaction sites as a sacrifice substance.

nodes.label: Grape Seed Procyanidins
nodes.summary: With tocopherols inhibited AGE formation by 90% in BSA-glucose assay.

nodes.label: Tocopherol
nodes.summary: Vitamin E forms combined with procyanidins for anti-glycation.

nodes.label: Fructosamine-3-Kinase
nodes.summary: FN3K: skin's own de-glycation enzyme system stimulated by Bay cedar extract.

nodes.label: Bay Cedar Extract
nodes.summary: Guazuma ulmifolia extract stimulating FN3K, partially restoring glycation damage; amplifies glycation decrease at acidic pH.

nodes.label: Chrysophyllum Extract
nodes.summary: Inhibits type I collagen and vimentin glycation, preserving fibroblast motility and contractility.

nodes.label: Azeloyl Tetrapeptide
nodes.summary: Antioxidant anti-glycation peptide reducing fibroblast AGE formation ~50%; improved wrinkles and elasticity after six weeks.

nodes.label: Tripeptide-9 Citrulline
nodes.summary: Peptide chelating copper and preventing methylglyoxal reaction with DNA in vitro.

nodes.label: C-Xyloside
nodes.summary: GAG synthesis stimulator tested with blueberry extract on diabetic skin over 12 weeks.

nodes.label: Blueberry Extract
nodes.summary: Antioxidant chosen for anti-glycation potential in diabetic skin study.

nodes.label: Amadoriases
nodes.summary: Deglycating enzymes evidenced in vertebrates; not yet led to true AGE-breakers.

nodes.label: Alagebrium
nodes.summary: Former prescription AGE-breaker drug candidate that failed to reach market.

nodes.label: Albizia Julibrissin Extract
nodes.summary: 'Night sleeper' extract with preventive and curative anti-glycation: inhibits BSA glycation ~50%, reduces CML 43%, explant AGEs -23.4%, maintains glyoxalase-1 and proteasome activity; reduces skin fatigue.

nodes.label: Piper Longum Fruit Extract
nodes.summary: Promotes blood circulation, keratinocyte proliferation, filaggrin synthesis, inhibits melanin synthesis and glycation.

nodes.label: Dark Eye Circles
nodes.summary: Skin problem linked to poor blood circulation; assessed in Albizia self-assessment.

nodes.label: Autophagy
nodes.summary: Cellular self-eating pathway degrading long-lived proteins and damaged organelles; takes over when proteasome is overwhelmed; target for detoxifying actives.

nodes.label: LC3-II
nodes.summary: Specific autophagy marker increasing after H2O2 oxidative stress recovery.

nodes.label: Oxidized/Carbonylated Proteins
nodes.summary: Noxious products accumulating with stress and age, reducing epidermal transparency; normally degraded by proteasome.

nodes.label: Calcitriol
nodes.summary: Vitamin D form preventing UV-induced senescence and DNA damage, activating proteasome; vitamin D excluded from EU cosmetics.

nodes.label: Diglycerol Phosphate
nodes.summary: DGP from marine prokaryote Archaeoglobus fulgidus; stimulates HSP27 associated with 26S proteasome.

nodes.label: HSP27
nodes.summary: Heat-shock protein directly associated with 26S proteasome.

nodes.label: Avocado Pulp Peptide Complex
nodes.summary: Stimulates collagen I and elastin, inhibits MMP1, activates LOX/LOXL, antioxidant, increases proteasome expression.

nodes.label: Matrix Metalloproteinases
nodes.summary: MMP1 activity inhibited by avocado peptide complex.

nodes.label: Cochlearia Extract
nodes.summary: Increases proteasome activity in H2O2-stressed fibroblasts, decreasing protein oxidation.

nodes.label: Olive Leaf Extract
nodes.summary: In blend with jujube and levan said to reactivate the proteasome.

nodes.label: Levan
nodes.summary: Tightening polysaccharide in proteasome-activating blend.

nodes.label: Candida Saitoana Ferment
nodes.summary: Fermentation broth extract increasing LC3 ~20%, reducing oxidized proteins and lipids, improving tone and radiance.

nodes.label: p53
nodes.summary: Apoptosis-inducing protein rapidly degraded by increased proteasome activity; link to cancer caveat.

nodes.label: Tyrosinase
nodes.summary: Melanogenic enzyme whose degradation may be accelerated by increased proteasome activity.

nodes.label: Shelterin Complex
nodes.summary: Telosome of TRF1, TRF2, POT1, RAP1, TIN2 and TPP1 essential for telomere function.

nodes.label: TRF2
nodes.summary: Telomeric-repeat binding factor-2 stabilizing telomeres; expression declines with senescence.

nodes.label: Senescence-Associated Beta-Galactosidase
nodes.summary: SA-bgal marker that increases in senescent cells.

nodes.label: Stress-Induced Premature Senescence
nodes.summary: SIPS: model inducing senescence by repeated weak oxidative stress (e.g., H2O2) for testing molecules.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Peroxide
nodes.summary: Used to simulate oxidative stress inducing senescence and telomere shortening; trace levels showed hormesis-like slowing of telomere shortening.

nodes.label: Stem Cells
nodes.summary: Stem-cell-ness correlates with telomere length; telomere loss may contribute to stem cell dysfunction.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle
nodes.summary: Anagen bulb shows high telomerase activity; bulge quiescent stem cells low.

nodes.label: Multivitamin Supplementation
nodes.summary: Oral multivitamins associated with 5% longer telomeres.

nodes.label: TA-65
nodes.summary: Astragalus-derived molecule claimed to lengthen telomeres via telomerase activation orally.

nodes.label: Gamma-Tocotrienol
nodes.summary: Increased fibroblast viability (optimum 40-80 µM), prevented H2O2-induced telomere shortening and telomerase loss.

nodes.label: Narcissus Tazetta Bulb Extract
nodes.summary: Dormant bulb extract slowing epidermal turnover, sparing telomeres.

nodes.label: Hydrolyzed Soy and Wheat Protein (IV10.008)
nodes.summary: Limited TRF-2 loss in senescent fibroblasts and reduced DNA double-strand breaks.

nodes.label: Scutellaria Baicalensis Extract
nodes.summary: Baicalin-standardized extract delaying telomere erosion, 10% more fibroblast doublings; improved roughness and elasticity clinically.

nodes.label: Red Algae Galactans
nodes.summary: Reduced stress-induced telomere shortening 65%; limited POT1 and TPP1 decline.

nodes.label: Geranylgeranylacetone
nodes.summary: GGA: synthetic isoprenoid delaying senescence; clinically decreased TEWL, rosacea, sunspots, pore size; increased moisturization and firmness.

nodes.label: Geranylgeranylpropanol
nodes.summary: GGP: maintained telomere length in pre-senescent cells (+1.45 kbp at 1.65 ppm).

nodes.label: Progerin
nodes.summary: Mutant lamin A protein causing progeria; produced in normal cells, activated by telomere damage during senescence.

nodes.label: Progeria
nodes.summary: Devastating premature aging disease from LMNA point mutation.

nodes.label: Hormesis
nodes.summary: Low-dose stress effect; trace H2O2 slows age-dependent telomere shortening.

nodes.label: Sirtuins and Skin
nodes.summary: Reviews the seven mammalian sirtuins as NAD+-dependent deacetylases, their nuclear (SIRT1, SIRT6) and mitochondrial (SIRT3-5) biochemistry, and how UVB and ozone disrupt sirtuin expression in keratinocytes. Discusses resveratrol as a sirtuin activator and nicotinamide as a potential inhibitor for hyperproliferative skin conditions.

nodes.label: SIRT1
nodes.summary: Nuclear sirtuin deacetylating histones for gene silencing, deacetylating BMAL-1, activating p53, attenuating FOXO; promotes keratinocyte differentiation.

nodes.label: SIRT3
nodes.summary: Mitochondrial sirtuin activating acetyl-CoA synthetase and SOD2 by deacetylation; decreased by ozone and disrupted by UVB in keratinocytes.

nodes.label: SIRT4
nodes.summary: Mitochondrial sirtuin upregulated by caloric restriction; inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase by ADP-ribosylation, reducing ATP; inversely expressed to SIRT3.

nodes.label: SIRT5
nodes.summary: Mitochondrial sirtuin deacetylating carbamoyl phosphate synthetase, regulating urea cycle.

nodes.label: SIRT6
nodes.summary: Nuclear chromatin-bound sirtuin aiding base excision and double-strand break repair, regulating glycolysis; knockout causes graying and fat loss; associates with telomeres.

nodes.label: SIRT7
nodes.summary: Sirtuin reported in the nucleolus.

nodes.label: SIRT2
nodes.summary: Cytoplasmic sirtuin.

nodes.label: NAD+
nodes.summary: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide cofactor for sirtuins; makes sirtuins sensitive to cellular metabolic state and caloric restriction.

nodes.label: 2'-O-Acetyl-ADP Ribose
nodes.summary: Unique reaction product formed when sirtuins transfer an acetyl group to NAD+.

nodes.label: Histone Deacetylation
nodes.summary: SIRT1 removal of acetyl groups from histones reducing chromatin polarity, causing condensation and gene silencing.

nodes.label: Circadian Rhythm
nodes.summary: Diurnal gene expression coordinated by CLOCK/BMAL-1; SIRT1 deacetylates BMAL-1 influencing skin cell rhythms.

nodes.label: CLOCK/BMAL-1 Complex
nodes.summary: Circadian heterodimer; CLOCK acetyltransferase acetylates BMAL-1; limited by SIRT1 deacetylation.

nodes.label: FOXO
nodes.summary: Forkhead box oxidative stress transcription factors attenuated by SIRT1, aiding survival.

nodes.label: DNA Repair
nodes.summary: Base excision and double-strand break repair aided by SIRT6; immediately affected by sirtuin expression changes.

nodes.label: Acetyl-CoA Synthetase
nodes.summary: AceCS2 activated by SIRT3, increasing oxidative phosphorylation and ATP.

nodes.label: Glutamate Dehydrogenase
nodes.summary: Inhibited by SIRT4 ADP-ribosylation, reducing alpha-ketoglutarate and ATP.

nodes.label: ATP
nodes.summary: Cellular energy; decreased in keratinocytes after UVB.

nodes.label: UVB Radiation
nodes.summary: Low non-cytotoxic UVB (10 mJ/cm2) abrogates SIRT3/SIRT4 expression, lowers ATP and raises H2O2 in keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Ozone
nodes.summary: Tropospheric ozone pollutant (0.4 ppm, 30 min) decreased SIRT3 in keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Psoriasis
nodes.summary: Hyperproliferative skin condition potentially improved by sirtuin inhibitors.

nodes.label: Epigenetics of Skin Aging
nodes.summary: Explains epigenetic principles (DNA methylation, chromatin remodeling and histone modification), their links to aging, epigenetic drift in aging skin illustrated by identical twins, DNA damage repair, cosmetic ingredients and dietary compounds as epigenetic modifiers (nutriepigenetics), and epigenetics as a possible unifying theory of aging.

nodes.label: Epigenome
nodes.summary: Totality of epigenetic tags 'running' the genome; varies by cell type; 98% of adult somatic cell genome silenced.

nodes.label: Human Genome Project
nodes.summary: International project completed 2003 finding only ~20,500 genes (<2% of genome), revealing mutations too rare to explain disease and aging.

nodes.label: Noncoding DNA
nodes.summary: 98% of genome once called 'junk DNA'; includes sequences governing when, where and how much genes are expressed.

nodes.label: DNA Methylation
nodes.summary: Addition of methyl groups to cytosine at CpG sites by DNMTs using SAM, silencing genes; with age CpG islands become hypermethylated and non-island sites globally hypomethylated.

nodes.label: DNA Methyltransferases
nodes.summary: DNMT1 (maintenance, most abundant), DNMT3A and DNMT3B add methyl groups to cytosines.

nodes.label: S-Adenosyl Methionine
nodes.summary: SAM: methyl donor for most DNMT activities; converted to SAH.

nodes.label: CpG Islands
nodes.summary: Clusters of CpG sites near promoter regions; <3% methylated in normal tissue; hypermethylated with age.

nodes.label: DNA Methylation Age (Epigenetic Clock)
nodes.summary: Age-associated methylation signatures correlate 0.96 with chronological age; ~80% more accurate than telomere-length clock.

nodes.label: Global Hypomethylation
nodes.summary: Age-related loss of methylation at non-island CpG sites; most important feature of aging cells.

nodes.label: Tumor Suppressor Genes
nodes.summary: Genes shut down by aberrant DNA methylation in almost all cancers.

nodes.label: Chromatin Remodeling
nodes.summary: Changing chromatin condensation between open euchromatin and silent heterochromatin; 98% of keratinocyte genome heterochromatic.

nodes.label: Chromatin
nodes.summary: Chromosomal complex of DNA, nucleosomes (eight histones) and RNA.

nodes.label: Euchromatin
nodes.summary: Loosely condensed transcriptionally active chromatin.

nodes.label: Heterochromatin
nodes.summary: Tightly condensed transcriptionally silent chromatin; telomeres are hypermethylated heterochromatin.

nodes.label: Histone Modification
nodes.summary: Acetylation, methylation, phosphorylation, ubiquitination and sumoylation of histone tails altering gene expression; methylation can be inherited.

nodes.label: Histone Acetyltransferase
nodes.summary: HAT: acetylates histones opening chromatin for gene expression; HAT/HDAC imbalance drives aging.

nodes.label: Histone Deacetylase
nodes.summary: HDAC: deacetylates histones tightening chromatin and silencing genes; at least 18 in humans including seven sirtuins.

nodes.label: Histone Methyltransferase
nodes.summary: HMT adds methyl groups to histones; reversible via LSD1, PAD4, JMJDs.

nodes.label: Noncoding RNA
nodes.summary: miRNA, siRNA, piRNA and lncRNA epigenetic regulators; a novel ncRNA binds DNMT1 preventing CEBPA methylation.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Drift
nodes.summary: Progressive deregulation of epigenetic marks with age, exacerbated by UV, smoking, stress, diet, alcohol; visible in twin studies.

nodes.label: Identical Twin Studies
nodes.summary: Monozygotic twins (Guyuron) show perceived age differences up to 11.25 years from smoking, sun, BMI and HRT differences.

nodes.label: Tobacco Smoking
nodes.summary: Causes baggy eyes, hollow cheeks, lines and large pores in twin studies; impairs HDAC2.

nodes.label: DNA Damage Response
nodes.summary: DDR pathway of repair enzymes (MMR, BER, NER) regulated epigenetically; works with p53; repair may remove epigenetic tags.

nodes.label: Nucleotide Excision Repair
nodes.summary: NER corrects complex damage such as UV-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers.

nodes.label: Cyclobutane Pyrimidine Dimers
nodes.summary: CPDs: most common UV DNA lesions forming at methylation sites; major source of sunlight mutations.

nodes.label: Base Excision Repair
nodes.summary: BER cuts out small chemically altered bases and replaces them.

nodes.label: Nrf2
nodes.summary: Transcription factor controlling endogenous antioxidants and phase II enzymes; downregulated with age; upregulated by some cosmetic ingredients and sulforaphane.

nodes.label: Human Longevity-Associated Genes
nodes.summary: 150 long-life variants of 70 genes found in ~80% of centenarians; form protein interaction networks.

nodes.label: Oryza Plant Meristem Cell Extract
nodes.summary: Rice-genus meristem cell suspension extract shown in vitro to restore youthful DNA methylation in aged fibroblasts; first US-patented epigenetic cosmetic ingredient.

nodes.label: Epigenetically Active Cosmetic Ingredients
nodes.summary: Ingredients modulating gene expression via epigenetic mechanisms; raise questions about timing, cell specificity, penetration and safety.

nodes.label: Nutriepigenetics
nodes.summary: Study of how dietary nutrients alter the epigenome; nutrition second only to environment in epigenetic impact.

nodes.label: One-Carbon Metabolism
nodes.summary: Folate-methionine cycle supplying methyl groups (folate, riboflavin, pyridoxine, cobalamin, choline, betaine, methionine) for DNA/histone methylation.

nodes.label: Folic Acid
nodes.summary: Methyl donor; with B12, choline and betaine fed to pregnant agouti mice methylated agouti gene.

nodes.label: Agouti Gene
nodes.summary: Mouse gene whose methylation by maternal supplements yields brown, healthier offspring; BPA decreases its methylation.

nodes.label: Bisphenol A
nodes.summary: Polycarbonate plastic compound in containers; decreased agouti gene methylation in mice, counteracted by methyl-rich foods.

nodes.label: Niacin
nodes.summary: B vitamin substrate of SIRT1, playing role in histone modification.

nodes.label: Pantothenic Acid
nodes.summary: Contributes to acetyl-CoA, source of acetyl groups for histone acetylation.

nodes.label: Biotin
nodes.summary: Covalently bound to histones (histone biotinylation; 11 sites in humans).

nodes.label: Genistein
nodes.summary: Phytoestrogenic isoflavone demethylating agent inhibiting DNMTs and HDACs and activating HATs; stronger than biochanin A and daidzein.

nodes.label: Epigallocatechin Gallate
nodes.summary: EGCG: major tea polyphenol; demethylating agent inhibiting DNMT1 and HATs, modulates miRNA, induces cancer apoptosis.

nodes.label: Sulforaphane
nodes.summary: Cruciferous isothiocyanate decreasing DNMTs, inhibiting HDACs, regulating Nrf2 and boosting phase II enzymes.

nodes.label: Curcumin
nodes.summary: Turmeric pigment inhibiting DNMT1, HDACs, HATs, miRNAs; HDAC inhibition more potent than valproic acid; restores HDAC2.

nodes.label: Diallyl Sulfide
nodes.summary: Allium organosulfur compound inhibiting HATs.

nodes.label: Retinol
nodes.summary: Vitamin A; retinoid signaling crosstalks with epigenetic factors; all-trans retinoic acid is a master epigenetic regulator.

nodes.label: Retinoic Acid
nodes.summary: All-trans RA: master epigenetic regulator of gene transcription.

nodes.label: Ascorbic Acid
nodes.summary: Vitamin C optimizes Tet enzymes removing DNA methyl groups in embryonic stem cells.

nodes.label: Vitamin D
nodes.summary: Recruits histone acetylases; via VDR regulates over 1000 genes involved in aging, inflammation and cancer.

nodes.label: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
nodes.summary: Dietary compound supported by modeling as HDAC inhibitor.

nodes.label: Polyphenols
nodes.summary: Dietary polyphenols (resveratrol, curcumin, quercetin, catechins) modulating NF-kB, MAPK and activating sirtuins.

nodes.label: Heat Shock Factor 1
nodes.summary: HSF1 transcription factor regulated by SIRT1 elevating heat shock protein chaperones.

nodes.label: Epigenetics as Unifying Theory of Aging
nodes.summary: Proposal that all aging theories (cross-linking, glycation, inflammation, telomere, free radical, mitochondrial, stem cell depletion, membrane) are rooted in epigenetic mechanisms.

nodes.label: Protein-DNA Interactome
nodes.summary: Network connecting genes; seven sirtuins act as hubs in 25% of interactome, warranting caution in gene-targeted cosmetics.

nodes.label: Hyperpigmentation
nodes.summary: Aging-skin sign with epigenetic regulation; target for epigenetic treatments.

nodes.label: Chronobiology of the Skin: Circadian Rhythm and Clock Genes
nodes.summary: Describes the SCN master clock and peripheral clock genes (CLOCK/BMAL1, PER/CRY feedback loops), the health consequences of circadian desynchronization (shift-work cancers, aging), and skin circadian rhythms: daytime protection versus nighttime repair, proliferation and higher permeability. UVB downregulates skin clock genes and ATP rhythms, suggesting night-targeted anti-aging treatments.

nodes.label: Suprachiasmatic Nucleus
nodes.summary: Master clock in the hypothalamus (~20,000 neurons) receiving light cues via the retina and synchronizing peripheral clocks.

nodes.label: Clock Genes
nodes.summary: Peripheral molecular clocks present in nearly all cells (period, clock, cycle, timeless); expressed in human skin cells (shown 2000).

nodes.label: PER Genes
nodes.summary: Period genes (PER1-3), first clock gene identified 1971 in flies; PER protein peaks early evening; PER1 and PER2 are tumor suppressors.

nodes.label: Cryptochromes
nodes.summary: CRY1-2 repressors forming PER/CRY complex that blocks CLOCK/BMAL1 transactivation.

nodes.label: REV-ERB alpha
nodes.summary: Nuclear receptor rhythmically repressing BMAL1 transcription in a second feedback loop.

nodes.label: ROR alpha
nodes.summary: Clock-controlled gene activating BMAL1 transcription via ROR response elements.

nodes.label: Casein Kinase
nodes.summary: Phosphorylates PERs, regulating nuclear import and degradation.

nodes.label: Circadian Desynchronization
nodes.summary: Loss of synchrony of clock genes with earth's cycle due to stress, aging, shift work; induces genome instability, premature aging, cancer, obesity, diabetes.

nodes.label: Shift Work
nodes.summary: Associated with obesity, metabolic syndrome, elevated cortisol, breast and prostate cancer via circadian disruption and altered clock gene methylation.

nodes.label: Breast Cancer
nodes.summary: Increased in night-shift workers; differential promoter methylation of core circadian genes.

nodes.label: Skin Circadian Rhythm
nodes.summary: Daytime skin is thicker, higher pH and sebum for protection; at night higher temperature, blood flow, permeability, TEWL (~25% higher), DNA repair and 30-fold higher proliferation.

nodes.label: Sebum
nodes.summary: Production highest during the day, contributing to moisturization.

nodes.label: Transepidermal Water Loss
nodes.summary: About 25% higher at night than morning/afternoon, reflecting higher barrier permeability.

nodes.label: Skin Barrier
nodes.summary: Permeability higher at night; recovery rate lowest 8-11 p.m.

nodes.label: Alkyl Guanine Transferase
nodes.summary: AGT DNA repair enzyme with activity peaking at midnight.

nodes.label: XPA
nodes.summary: Xeroderma pigmentosum complementation group A repair protein peaking at night.

nodes.label: Cell Proliferation
nodes.summary: Skin cell proliferation 30-fold higher at night than noon, minimizing UV damage.

nodes.label: Chrono-Delivery
nodes.summary: Timing drug/cosmetic delivery to circadian phase; topical formulations more efficient at night; chemotherapy timing optimized.

nodes.label: Dermatitis
nodes.summary: Frequency and severity increased in clock-deficient models.

nodes.label: Itching
nodes.summary: Itch is higher at night.

nodes.label: Genome Instability
nodes.summary: Increased when circadian gene expression is uncoupled from cell cycle, promoting premature aging and cancer.

nodes.label: Stress, Sleep and Epigenetic Orthodontics
nodes.summary: Part 1 explains normal sleep stages, chronic stress via the HPA axis, insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea, and how poor sleep, cortisol, epinephrine, reduced growth hormone and free radicals accelerate skin aging; therapies include CBT, sleep hygiene, CPAP and oral appliances. Part 2 presents epigenetic orthodontics, using functional appliances and mechanotransduction to remodel craniofacial bone as nonsurgical facial anti-aging.

nodes.label: Sleep Stages
nodes.summary: 4-5 cycles of 90-120 min: N1 (~5%), N2 (~50%), N3 deep sleep (~20%) and REM (20-25%).

nodes.label: Deep Sleep (Stage N3)
nodes.summary: Slow-wave sleep (~20% of total) when the major human growth hormone pulse is released.

nodes.label: REM Sleep
nodes.summary: Dreaming sleep (20-25%) consolidating memory; disrupted by high nighttime cortisol.

nodes.label: Human Growth Hormone
nodes.summary: Pituitary 'anti-aging hormone' released in stage 3 sleep for tissue repair; deficiency causes thin, wrinkle-prone skin.

nodes.label: Chronic Stress
nodes.summary: Long-term overactivation of sympathetic nervous system and HPA axis; causes weight gain, hair loss, hypertension, and premature aging.

nodes.label: Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis
nodes.summary: Fight-or-flight cascade: CRF and vasopressin to pituitary ACTH to adrenal cortisol, epinephrine, norepinephrine; negative feedback by cortisol.

nodes.label: Sympathetic Nervous System
nodes.summary: 'Fight or flight' branch of the autonomic nervous system most relevant to skin.

nodes.label: Cortisol
nodes.summary: Glucocorticoid stress hormone; excess breaks down skin collagen (loss 10x greater than other tissues), reduces skin regeneration, disrupts REM; linked to adult acne.

nodes.label: Epinephrine
nodes.summary: Adrenaline; binds alpha-2-adrenergic receptors constricting skin arteries; elevated levels delay wound healing and re-epithelialization.

nodes.label: Norepinephrine
nodes.summary: Neurotransmitter/hormone released by adrenals in stress response.

nodes.label: Adrenocorticotropic Hormone
nodes.summary: Pituitary hormone activating adrenal glands; elevated in chronic insomnia.

nodes.label: Insomnia
nodes.summary: Inability to sleep despite opportunity; primary or secondary, onset (>30 min latency) or maintenance; chronic insomnia is a 24-hour hyperarousal disorder with high cortisol and ACTH.

nodes.label: Obstructive Sleep Apnea
nodes.summary: Airway collapse during sleep causing oxygen desaturation, HPA activation, fragmented sleep; graded by AHI; increases oxidative stress, reduces growth hormone; more prevalent with age.

nodes.label: Apnea-Hypopnea Index
nodes.summary: Events per hour of sleep: <=5 normal, 5-15 mild, 15-30 moderate, >30 severe OSA.

nodes.label: Polysomnography
nodes.summary: Standard overnight sleep study for diagnosis; home tests, actigraphy and pulse-oximetry also used.

nodes.label: Melatonin
nodes.summary: Sleep-promoting hormone rising in evening; suppressed by light; decrease can cause onset insomnia.

nodes.label: Wound Healing
nodes.summary: Delayed by stress-elevated epinephrine; beta-blockers improve burn re-epithelialization.

nodes.label: Beta-Blockers
nodes.summary: Beta-adrenergic antagonists (e.g., timolol) proposed as topical anti-aging therapies; improve burn wound re-epithelialization.

nodes.label: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia
nodes.summary: Non-medical therapy building understanding of insomnia and good sleep habits.

nodes.label: Sleep Hygiene
nodes.summary: Regular schedule, no afternoon caffeine (half-life ~4.9 h), no alcohol or smoking before bed, dark quiet room, exercise not near bedtime.

nodes.label: Caffeine
nodes.summary: Adenosine antagonist delaying sleep onset; half-life about 4.9 hours.

nodes.label: Adenosine
nodes.summary: Builds up in brain driving homeostatic sleep drive; blocked by caffeine.

nodes.label: CPAP Therapy
nodes.summary: Continuous positive airway pressure 'pneumatic splint'; gold standard OSA therapy, but compliance issues.

nodes.label: Oral Appliance Therapy
nodes.summary: Custom dental device advancing mandible to open airway for mild/moderate OSA or CPAP-noncompliant patients.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Orthodontics
nodes.summary: 'Nonsurgical plastic surgery' using functional appliances to upregulate methylated 'sleepy' genes via mechanotransduction, remodeling craniofacial bone for symmetry and smoother skin.

nodes.label: Dento-Facial Orthopedics
nodes.summary: Removable night appliances applying forces to teeth and craniofacial bones to treat malocclusion and underdeveloped skeletal structures.

nodes.label: Functional (Formational) Appliances
nodes.summary: Dental appliances creating bite imbalance and pressure to trigger mechanotransduction and bone remodeling.

nodes.label: Mechanotransduction
nodes.summary: Cell signaling by mechanical stimuli (stretch, deformation) detected by periodontal mechanoreceptors, changing gene expression and inducing osteogenesis.

nodes.label: Craniofacial Bone Remodeling
nodes.summary: New bone deposition at sutures, cheekbones and mandible supporting skin, reducing wrinkles, sagging and dark circles.

nodes.label: Upper Airway Resistance Syndrome
nodes.summary: Sleep breathing dysfunction from narrow V-shaped maxilla in ages 18-40 causing arousals, daytime sleepiness and mood disorders.

nodes.label: Acne
nodes.summary: Adult acne linked to abnormal cortisol rhythm.

nodes.label: Botulinum Toxin
nodes.summary: Cholinergic modulator proposed as possible stress-related anti-aging therapy.

nodes.label: Mifepristone
nodes.summary: Glucocorticoid blocker proposed as possible topical anti-aging therapy.

nodes.label: Valsartan
nodes.summary: Angiotensin receptor blocker proposed as possible topical anti-aging therapy.
